label: Gentleness and Meekness
framing: Gentleness is not weakness, and meekness is not timidity. Scripture means by them a strength held under control, power that chooses restraint, and it puts the gentle answer forward as the thing that turns away wrath where a harsh word only feeds it.
cultural: The Greek word for meekness, praotes, was used of a powerful horse that had been trained, all its strength intact but now answering to the reins, so meekness named not the lack of force but force brought under control. This cut hard against a Greco-Roman world that admired the assertive and the dominant and looked down on the yielding. Into that, Jesus called the meek blessed and the inheritors of the earth, and described himself as gentle and lowly in heart, redefining greatness as the strength that does not need to crush.
historical: The church held this strange virtue at its center, since its Lord had ridden into the city on a donkey rather than a war horse and answered his accusers with silence. Francis of Assisi in the thirteenth century became its emblem, disarming enemies by refusing their weapons, and the long tradition of the gentle answer ran through pastors and reformers who learned that you cannot bully a soul into faith. Gentleness, the church found, persuades where force only hardens.
application: Watch your tone with the people closest to you, where harshness most easily becomes a habit and does the deepest damage. Aim for the soft answer in the heat, since it costs you a moment of pride and saves you a week of repair. Treat the failing and the weak as you would want to be treated in your own falling, with a strength that lifts rather than crushes. And know that gentleness is not having no fire but keeping your hand on the reins of it.

verses.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
verses.where: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger. The site's note says the chapter opens here and keeps returning to the tongue, soothing or perverse, timely or rash. The one who answers gently often ends the fight the harsh word would have started.

verses.text: Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
verses.where: Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone. The site's note sets it among the Hezekiah collection's sayings on words well spoken, restraint and self-control. Gentleness, in Proverbs, is not the weak option; it reaches what force cannot.

verses.text: Now Moses was a very humble man, more so than any man on the face of the earth.
verses.where: When Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses and ask whether the LORD speaks only through him, the narrator says Moses was a very humble man, more than anyone on earth. The site's note on the chapter says that when Miriam is struck with a skin disease, Moses prays for her healing. The man who faced Pharaoh did not defend himself against his own family; he prayed for them.

verses.text: He tends His flock like a shepherd; He gathers the lambs in His arms and carries them close to His heart. He gently leads the nursing ewes.
verses.where: Isaiah says the LORD comes with a ruling arm, and like a shepherd gathers the lambs in his arms and gently leads the nursing ewes. The site's note says the God who comes is described in two images held together, warrior and shepherd, and that the same arm does both. Gentleness in God is strength choosing how to hold.

verses.text: “Say to the Daughter of Zion, ‘See, your King comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’”
verses.where: Matthew says Jesus' entry into Jerusalem fulfills the prophet's word: your King comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey. The site's note says the quotation interprets everything that follows: this is a king, and a humble one. The plain note asks what kind of king we want, one with chariots or one who comes gentle, to make peace.

verses.text: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
verses.where: Jesus says the meek are blessed, for they will inherit the earth. The site's note says the saying is nearly a quotation of Psalm 37:11, a psalm that urges the faithful not to fret over the wicked, because the land will belong to those who wait for the LORD. Meekness here is trust that does not need to grab.

verses.text: Let your gentleness be apparent to all. The Lord is near.
verses.where: Paul tells the church to let their gentleness be apparent to all, for the Lord is near. The site's note on the chapter sets the call to be gentle beside rejoicing, praying instead of worrying, and filling the mind with what is good. The nearness of the Lord is the reason given for a gentle life.

verses.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
verses.where: Gentleness is named in the fruit of the Spirit, with love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness and self-control. The site's plain note asks what helps fruit grow, and answers: not straining, but staying close to its source. Gentleness is grown more than it is forced.

verses.text: But in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord. Always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks you the reason for the hope that is in you. But respond with gentleness and respect, keeping a clear conscience, so that those who slander you may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ.
verses.where: Peter tells believers to be ready to give the reason for their hope, but with gentleness and respect, keeping a clear conscience. The site's plain note says this is not a call to start fights, corner people or treat every conversation as a debate to win. It adds that it is no failure to say, I do not know, but here is why I trust Christ.

verses.text: But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.
verses.where: James says the wisdom from above is pure, peace-loving, gentle, accommodating and full of mercy. The site's note says he sets it against earthly wisdom marked by jealousy and selfish ambition, and the plain note says he names those things as found in every heart, his own included. Gentleness is one of the ways true wisdom shows itself.

misread.taken: Be kind to everyone and gently reprove those who oppose you is used to tell someone who has been harmed to be gentle and stay quiet, or a church to handle harm softly and privately.
misread.says: The site's plain note says Paul is describing how to correct people who oppose the truth, with patience rather than anger or humiliation, which rules out bullying and shaming. But gentleness never means hiding harm. These verses must never be used to silence someone who has been harmed, to protect someone who has done harm, or to tell a victim to be gentle and stay quiet, and abuse and other crimes are reported to the police and the proper authorities.
misread.text: And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing. He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth.

whole: Gentleness is easy to mistake for weakness. A gentle man can look soft; a gentle woman can look easy to walk over. Many people learned in hard homes or hard workplaces that the loud win and the gentle get used. Others are gentle with strangers and harsh with the people closest to them, or soft in manner and cutting in what they actually say. Online, where everyone argues, gentleness can look like losing.

Scripture means something sturdier. Moses, who faced Pharaoh and led a nation, is called a very humble man, and when his own brother and sister turned on him he prayed for Miriam's healing. Isaiah describes the LORD coming with a ruling arm and, with the same arm, gathering lambs and gently leading the nursing ewes. Jesus entered Jerusalem as a king, gentle and riding on a donkey. Gentleness in the Bible is strength that chooses not to crush. Part of why we lack it is fear: we push because we are afraid of being pushed. Part is pride. James sets gentle wisdom against jealousy and selfish ambition, and most of us know which of the two has been doing the talking.

So the Bible's wisdom is to practise gentleness where it costs. A gentle answer turns away wrath, Proverbs says, and a gentle tongue can break a bone, which means gentleness is often more effective, not less. Peter tells believers to give the reason for their hope with gentleness and respect, and the site's plain note says that is not a call to win arguments. Paul tells Timothy to correct opponents gently, hoping they come home rather than wanting to defeat them. Gentleness is a fruit of the Spirit, grown by staying close to its source rather than by straining. And gentleness never means hiding harm: the site's plain note on 2 Timothy 2 says these verses must never be used to silence someone who has been harmed, and the Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

The hope Scripture gives is a gentle King and a promise. Jesus called the meek blessed and said they will inherit the earth, words drawn from a psalm that tells the faithful not to fret over the wicked. Paul says, let your gentleness be apparent to all; the Lord is near. The gentle are not losing. They are trusting that the earth belongs to God, and that he does not need them to grab it.
deep.sit: Where are you gentle in manner but harsh in what you say, or harsh because you are afraid of being pushed, and what would a gentle answer sound like there this week?

prayer.lead: The psalm Jesus echoed when he blessed the meek. The site's plain note says it does not tell you that what makes you fret does not matter; it says your anger will not fix it, and God will.
prayer.text: Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for Him; do not fret when men prosper in their ways, when they carry out wicked schemes. Refrain from anger and abandon wrath; do not fret—it can only bring harm. For the evildoers will be cut off, but those who hope in the LORD will inherit the land. Yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more; though you look for them, they will not be found. But the meek will inherit the land and delight in abundant prosperity.

careLines.text: But gentleness never means hiding harm.
These verses must never be used to silence someone who has been harmed, to protect someone who has done harm, or to tell a victim to be ‘gentle’ and stay quiet.
